title: Highly selective visual circuits in mouse frontal cortex
desc: It is thought that elementary stimulus encoding happens primarily in the sensory cortex. We found that frontal cortex neurons in awake mice show highly selective visual spatial receptive fields, akin to the visual cortex. These neurons were most sensitive to binocular visual space, required retinotopically aligned V1 input and sent functional axonal feedback throughout the visual cortex, particularly binocular V1. This reveals a cortex-wide circuit suitable for selective feedback control of spatial vision. The authors identify neurons in the frontal cortex of awake mice with highly selective visual receptive fields. These neurons prioritize encoding of binocular visual space, require V1 input and provide functional feedback throughout the visual cortex.
